blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). Scenario: an agent looks up an address that matches no customer; `errorHandler` in src/server.ts runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, so the typed e-mail address (personal data, possibly of a non-customer) lands in the application logs with no retention rule (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), 5(1)(e)). The same applies, to a lesser degree, to the customer id in `no customer ${id}` at src/support.ts:32.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
user: {
  id: String(customer.id),
  name: customer.name,
  email: customer.email,
  phone: customer.phone,
  birthDate: customer.birth_date,
  address: customer.address,
},
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — the id and the name ("greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to"); drop `phone`, `birthDate` and `address` (and `email` unless the plan states why the vendor needs it). Scenario: any signed-in customer opening the chat causes GET /chat/settings to hand their phone number, date of birth and postal address to the browser-side widget and so to the third-party processor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address to greet by name

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The purpose is that agents no longer ask customers who they are; select and return only the fields an agent needs for that (likely id, name, e-mail) instead of the whole `Customer` with birth date and address, which `res.json(...)` at src/routes.ts:7 sends to the support console as is (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Confidence is low: what the support console actually needs to display is not stated in the plan.
findings.title: Support lookup returns the full customer record

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change starts sharing customer data with Helply. Confirm a processor agreement exists (GDPR Art. 28), the record of processing is updated (Art. 30), and whether data is transferred outside the EEA (Chapter V). The proposal names the vendor but not its status.
findings.title: Helply as a new processor is not identified
